2027-12-12.a: The Preaching of Saint John the Baptist by Rembrandt, about 1634–35, painted in shades of brown as a study. A great crowd of every kind of listener, some rapt, some bored, gathers around the prophet. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

2027-12-13.b: A young Christian of Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means 'light', and her feast falls in the darkest days of the year.
2027-12-13.a: The Burial of Saint Lucy by Caravaggio, 1608, painted in Syracuse while he was on the run. Two huge gravediggers dwarf the mourners around her body. It was painted for the church of Santa Lucia al Sepolcro, built over the place of her burial.

2027-12-14.t: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church
2027-12-14.b: A Carmelite friar who worked with St. Teresa of Ávila to reform the order. His poems, including The Dark Night, are among the treasures of Spanish literature. A Doctor of the Church.
2027-12-14.a: Christ Crucified with a Carmelite friar, probably John of the Cross, attributed to Agustín del Castillo, early 1600s. John's own small drawing of Christ on the cross, seen from above, later inspired Salvador Dalí. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts of Córdoba.

2027-12-15.t: Wednesday of the third week of Advent
2027-12-15.b: “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good news preached to them.”
2027-12-15.a: Saint John the Baptist in Prison Visited by Two Disciples by Giovanni di Paolo, 1455–60, one of a series of panels on John's life. John sends his disciples through the barred window to ask, 'Are you the one who is to come?' It is in the Art Institute of Chicago.

2027-12-16.t: Thursday of the third week of Advent
2027-12-16.b: “I tell you, among those born of women none is greater than John; yet he who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
2027-12-16.a: The Appearance of Christ Before the People by Alexander Ivanov, 1837–57, a canvas more than seven meters wide that took him twenty years. John the Baptist points to the distant figure of Christ: 'Prepare the way of the Lord.' It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

2027-12-17.by: Circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans
2027-12-17.b: “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.”
2027-12-17.a: The Tree of Jesse, about 1500, from the circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans in Haarlem. The kings of Israel sit in the branches of a tree growing from the sleeping Jesse, with the Virgin and Child at the top. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

2027-12-18.b: “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.”
2027-12-18.a: The Dream of Saint Joseph by Georges de La Tour, about 1640. By the light of a single candle, a child-like angel touches the sleeping Joseph's arm. It is in the Museum of Arts, Nantes.

2027-12-19.b: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!”
2027-12-19.a: The Visitation by Jacopo Pontormo, about 1528–29. Mary and Elizabeth embrace in a swirl of brilliant color, watched by two women who seem to be their own doubles. It is in the church of San Michele at Carmignano, near Florence.

2027-12-20.b: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.”
2027-12-20.a: The Annunciation by Jan van Eyck, about 1434–36. Gabriel greets Mary in a dim Romanesque church, and their words are written in gold between them; Mary's answer is painted upside down so that God can read it. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

2027-12-21.t: Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church
2027-12-21.b: A Dutch Jesuit whose catechisms renewed Catholic life in Germany after the Reformation. A Doctor of the Church.
2027-12-21.a: Saint Peter Canisius, an anonymous portrait. The Dutch Jesuit's catechisms went through hundreds of editions in his lifetime and he was called the second apostle of Germany.

2027-12-22.b: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden. For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.”
2027-12-22.a: The Madonna of the Magnificat by Sandro Botticelli, about 1483. Mary writes the words of her song in a book held by angels, while the Child guides her hand. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.

2027-12-23.b: A professor at the University of Kraków, known for his learning and his great generosity to the poor.
2027-12-23.a: A Miracle of Saint John of Kanty by Taddeo Kuntze, about 1767. The Kraków professor was known for giving away his own clothes and food to the poor. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.

2027-12-24.b: “Through the tender mercy of our God, when the day shall dawn upon us from on high to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
2027-12-24.a: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds by Thomas Cole, 1833–34, founder of the Hudson River School. The angel's light breaks over a vast moonlit landscape. It is in the Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, Virginia.

2027-12-25.b: Christmas: the Son of God is born of the Virgin Mary in a stable at Bethlehem and laid in a manger, while angels sing to shepherds in the fields.
2027-12-25.a: The Adoration of the Child by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. All the light comes from the baby. Badly damaged by a car bomb outside the Uffizi in 1993, it was restored and hangs again in the Uffizi, Florence.

2027-12-26.t: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph
2027-12-26.b: A feast of the home at Nazareth, where Jesus grew 'in wisdom and age and grace' with Mary and Joseph. It is kept in the octave of Christmas as a model for every family.
2027-12-26.a: The Doni Tondo by Michelangelo, about 1506, his only finished panel painting. It was made for the wedding of Agnolo Doni in Florence. The Child passes between Mary and Joseph, with nude youths behind and the infant John the Baptist. It is in the Uffizi, still in its original carved frame.

2027-12-27.b: The beloved disciple, who leaned on Jesus at the Last Supper and stood at the foot of the cross. The Gospel, letters and Revelation are attributed to him.
2027-12-27.a: Saint John on Patmos by Hieronymus Bosch, about 1489. John gazes at a vision of the Woman clothed with the sun while a little devil tries to steal his ink. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

2027-12-28.b: The little boys of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. They are honored as the first to die for him.
2027-12-28.a: The Massacre of the Innocents by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1638, one of two he painted of the subject. Mothers fight Herod's soldiers for their children as cherubs bring the martyrs' crowns from above. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.

2027-12-29.t: Saint Thomas Becket, Bishop and Martyr
2027-12-29.b: Archbishop of Canterbury and former chancellor to King Henry II, murdered in his cathedral for defending the freedom of the Church.
2027-12-29.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Thomas Becket by Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre, 1748. The king's knights strike down the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral. It is in the church of Notre-Dame-de-la-Nativité de Bercy, Paris.

2027-12-30.t: Sixth Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord
2027-12-30.b: “Coming up at that very hour she gave thanks to God, and spoke of him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.”
2027-12-30.a: An Old Woman Reading, probably the Prophetess Anna, by Rembrandt, 1631. Light falls on the old woman's hand resting on the page of Scripture. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

2027-12-31.b: Pope during the reign of Constantine, when the Church emerged from persecution. In his time the first great basilicas of Rome were built and the Council of Nicaea was held.
2027-12-31.a: The Legend of Saint Sylvester by Agnolo Gaddi, about 1380–85. Legend tells how the pope tamed a dragon that was poisoning Rome. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
